h⁡(k,k,k)h(k,k,k) can now be brought to the row-echelon form by the sequence of elementary row-transformations given by

R2↔R1,R3→ω​R3−R1,R4→ω2​R4−R1\displaystyle R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{1},R_{3}\rightarrow\omega R_{3}-R_{1},R_{4}\rightarrow\omega^{2}R_{4}-R_{1}
R3→u​ω​ζ​R3−λ​ζ∗​R2,R4→R4​u−R2​ρ\displaystyle R_{3}\rightarrow u\omega\zeta R_{3}-\lambda\zeta^{*}R_{2},R_{4}\rightarrow R_{4}u-R_{2}\rho
R4=−u​ω​(ζ​ρ​(ω+1)−ζ∗​λ​ω)​R4+u​ζ​ω2​(ζ∗​λ+ζ​ρ)​R3.\displaystyle\begin{aligned} R_{4}&=-u\omega\left(\zeta\rho(\omega+1)-\zeta^{*}\lambda\omega\right)R_{4}\\ &+u\zeta\omega^{2}\left(\zeta^{*}\lambda+\zeta\rho\right)R_{3}.\end{aligned}

in conjunction with the using the identities ω3=1\omega^{3}=1, ζr∗=ζ∗\zeta r*=\zeta^{*} and r​r∗=1rr^{*}=1.The result of the row transformations is

(ζ∗​v0ζ∗​ρ​r​ωζ​λ​r∗​ω0ζ​uζ​u​ω2ζ​u​ω00ζ​u​(ω+1)​(ζ∗​λ+ζ​ρ)ζ​u​(ζ∗​λ+ζ​ρ)0000)\displaystyle\left(\begin{array}[]{cccc}\zeta^{*}v&0&\zeta^{*}\rho r\omega&\zeta\lambda r^{*}\omega\\ 0&\zeta u&\zeta u\omega^{2}&\zeta u\omega\\ 0&0&\zeta u(\omega+1)\left(\zeta^{*}\lambda+\zeta\rho\right)&\zeta u\left(\zeta^{*}\lambda+\zeta\rho\right)\\ 0&0&0&0\\ \end{array}\right)

The appearance of the 00 in the last diagonal element establishes that the maximum rank of h⁡(k,k,k)h(k,k,k) can be 33.

The analysis need not be repeated for the HM​F​TH_{M}FT at other gapless points like (−k,k,k),(k,−k,k)(-k,k,k),(k,-k,k) etc. All of h⁡(±k,±k,±k)h(\pm k,\pm k,\pm k) are related to h⁡(k,k,k)h(k,k,k) by elementary “rank-preserving” row and column transformations. h⁡(−k,k,k)h(-k,k,k) can be obtained from h⁡(k,k,k)h(k,k,k) by the transformations

R1↔R2,R3↔R4,\displaystyle R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2},R_{3}\leftrightarrow R_{4},
C1↔C2,C3↔C4,\displaystyle C_{1}\leftrightarrow C_{2},C_{3}\leftrightarrow C_{4},
R4→r∗​C4,C4→r​C4,\displaystyle R_{4}\rightarrow r^{*}C_{4},C_{4}\rightarrow rC_{4}, (209)

followed by two re-identifications: u↔vu\leftrightarrow v, which have been considered independent complex numbers in the proof; and ω↔ω2\omega\leftrightarrow\omega^{2} which survive the important properties ω3=1\omega^{3}=1 and 1+ω+ω2=01+\omega+\omega^{2}=0. h⁡(k,−k,k)h(k,-k,k) can be obtained in turn from h⁡(−k,k,k)h(-k,k,k) by the transformations

R2→R3,R3→R4,R4→R2,\displaystyle R_{2}\rightarrow R_{3},R_{3}\rightarrow R_{4},R_{4}\rightarrow R_{2}, (210)
C2→C3,C3→C4,C4→C2,\displaystyle C_{2}\rightarrow C_{3},C_{3}\rightarrow C_{4},C_{4}\rightarrow C_{2}, (211)
R1→ω2​R1,C1→ω2​C1.\displaystyle R_{1}\rightarrow\omega^{2}R_{1},C_{1}\rightarrow\omega^{2}C_{1}. (212)

h⁡(k,k,−k)h(k,k,-k) can be obtained from h⁡(−k,k,k)h(-k,k,k) by the transformations

R2→R4,R4→R3,R3→R2,\displaystyle R_{2}\rightarrow R_{4},R_{4}\rightarrow R_{3},R_{3}\rightarrow R_{2}, (213)
C2→C4,C4→C3,C3→C2,\displaystyle C_{2}\rightarrow C_{4},C_{4}\rightarrow C_{3},C_{3}\rightarrow C_{2}, (214)
R1→ω​R1,C1→ω​C1.\displaystyle R_{1}\rightarrow\omega R_{1},C_{1}\rightarrow\omega C_{1}. (215)

This completes the proof that h⁡(±k,±k,±k)h(\pm k,\pm k,\pm k) has a maximum rank of 33, and consequently, HM​F​T​(±k,±k,±k)H_{M}FT(\pm k,\pm k,\pm k) has two gapless bands which are protected by projective symmetries against the addition of arbitrarily long-ranged terms in the mean-field ansatz.

C.3 𝖴⁡(1)\mathsf{U}(1)

The 𝖴⁡(1)\mathsf{U}(1) spin liquid mean field ansatz has the following form:

Ui​j=i​Ui​j0​τ0+Ui​jz​τz,U_{ij}=iU^{0}_{ij}\tau_{0}+U^{z}_{ij}\tau_{z}, (216)

dictated by the fact that the ansatz is invariant under the 𝖴⁡(1)\mathsf{U}(1) IGG gauge transformation. We would like to investigate how the PSG solutions we obtained constrain the nearest neighbor mean field ansatz by subjecting them to the following test:

∀g∈𝖯​21​3×𝖹2𝒯:G^g​g^​(Ui​j)=Ui​j.\displaystyle\forall g\in\mathsf{P}2_{1}3\times\mathsf{Z}^{\mathcal{T}}_{2}:\hat{G}_{g}\hat{g}(U_{ij})=U_{ij}. (217)

Among the PSGs we have, we first study the class in which A=0A=0. After enumerating all the conditions imposed by the PSG, we arrive at the following nearest neighbor mean field ansatz in the class where A=0A=0.:

Ui=λ​τz,where ​i∈{1,…,12}.U_{i}=\lambda\tau_{z},\quad\text{where }i\in\{1,\dots,12\}. (218)

Next we would like to argue that, when A≠0A\neq 0, there would be no nearest neighbor mean field ansatz. We write U1/3≡i​𝔘1/3​exp⁡[i​φ1/3​τz]U_{1/3}\equiv i\mathfrak{U}_{1/3}\exp[i\varphi_{1/3}\tau_{z}]. The TRS conditions on these two bonds give:

2​φ1+A=π,φ3=π/2.2\varphi_{1}+A=\pi,\quad\varphi_{3}=\pi/2. (219)

However, the condition G^b​g^b​(U1)=U1\hat{G}_{b}\hat{g}_{b}(U_{1})=U_{1} gives us:

φ3+2​A+4​ϕ3=φ1.\varphi_{3}+2A+4\phi_{3}=\varphi_{1}. (220)

We time the above equation by 22, and combined with the last two relations, we would immediately arrive at 5​A=05A=0. Note that we had 3​A=03A=0. Thus the ansatz does not vanish only when A=0A=0.

We conclude that we obtain only one nearest neighbor 𝖴⁡(1)\mathsf{U}(1) mean field ansatz:

Uζ\displaystyle\quad U_{\zeta} =λ​τz,ζ∈{1,…,12}\displaystyle=\lambda\tau_{z},\quad\zeta\in\{1,\dots,12\}
as\displaystyle\quad a_{s} =ω​τz,i∈{α,…,δ}.\displaystyle=\omega\tau_{z},\quad i\in\{\alpha,\dots,\delta\}. (221)
